claims.text: Bactericidal beta-lactams (mechanism unknown, perhaps activating autolytic enzymes that destroy the cell wall).
claims.quote: Penicillins are beta-lactam antibiotics that are bactericidal by unknown mechanisms but perhaps by activating autolytic enzymes that destroy the cell wall in some bacteria.

claims.text: Clavulanate or sulbactam extends amoxicillin/ampicillin to MSSA, H. influenzae, M. catarrhalis, Bacteroides, E. coli, K. pneumoniae.
claims.quote: The addition of a beta-lactamase inhibitor (clavulanate or sulbactam) allows use against methicillin-sensitive staphylococci, H. influenzae, Moraxella catarrhalis, Bacteroides species, E. coli, and K. pneumoniae.
claims.locator: Indications for Penicillins › Amoxicillin and ampicillin

claims.text: AECOPD: amoxicillin (usually with clavulanate), a macrolide or doxycycline for 7–14 days, by local sensitivities.
claims.quote: The choice of antibiotic is dictated by local patterns of bacterial sensitivity and patient history. Macrolides (eg, azithromycin), amoxicillin (usually with clavulanic acid), or tetracyclines (eg, doxycycline) is given for 7 to 14 days.

claims.text: Adult LRTI: amoxicillin 875 mg q12h or 500 mg q8h;
claims.quote: Lower Respiratory Tract | Mild/Moderate or Severe | 875 mg every 12 hours or 500 mg every 8 hours
claims.locator: 2.2 Dosage for Adults and Pediatric Patients

claims.text: amoxicillin/clavulanate 875 mg q12h or 500 mg q8h
claims.quote: | Severe infections and infections of the respiratory tract | one 875 mg tablet a of Amoxicillin and Clavulanate Potassium every 12 hours or one 500 mg tablet b,c of Amoxicillin and Clavulanate Potassium every 8 hours

claims.text: (take at the start of a meal).
claims.quote: To minimize the potential for gastrointestinal intolerance, Amoxicillin and Clavulanate Potassium should be taken at the start of a meal.

claims.text: Ampicillin/sulbactam 1.5–3 g IV every six hours.
claims.quote: The recommended adult dosage of UNASYN is 1.5 g (ampicillin 1 g and sulbactam 0.5 g) to 3 g (ampicillin 2 g and sulbactam 1 g) every six hours.

claims.text: Reduce most penicillins in severe renal insufficiency (not antistaphylococcal ones).
claims.quote: Because penicillins, except antistaphylococcal penicillins (eg, nafcillin, oxacillin, cloxacillin, dicloxacillin), reach high levels in urine, doses must be reduced in patients with severe renal insufficiency.

claims.text: Mostly hypersensitivity: immediate (anaphylaxis, urticaria, angioedema) or delayed (serum sickness, rashes, exfoliative dermatitis).
claims.quote: Most adverse effects are hypersensitivity reactions: - Immediate reactions: Anaphylaxis (which can cause death within minutes), urticaria and angioneurotic edema (in 1 to 5/10,000 injections), and death (in about 0.3/10,000 injections) - Delayed reactions: Serum sickness, rashes (eg, macular, papular, morbilliform), and exfoliative dermatitis

claims.text: Ampicillin/amoxicillin rash, and a non-allergic maculopapular rash in infectious mononucleosis (days 4–7).
claims.quote: Rashes occur more often with ampicillin and amoxicillin than with other penicillins. Patients with infectious mononucleosis often develop a nonallergic rash, typically maculopapular, usually beginning between days 4 and 7 of treatment.

claims.text: High doses: seizures (esp. renal insufficiency); nephritis, C. difficile diarrhea, Coombs+ hemolytic anemia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia.
claims.quote: Central nervous system toxicity (eg, seizures) if doses are high, especially in patients with renal insufficiency - Nephritis - Clostridioides (formerly Clostridium) difficile–induced diarrhea (pseudomembranous colitis) - Coombs-positive hemolytic anemia - Leukopenia - Thrombocytopenia
claims.locator: Adverse Effects of Penicillins › Other adverse effects

claims.text: Amox-clav and amp-sulbactam: hepatitis/cholestatic jaundice (usually reversible).
claims.quote: Hepatic dysfunction, including hepatitis and cholestatic jaundice has been associated with the use of UNASYN. Hepatic toxicity is usually reversible; however, deaths have been reported.

claims.text: Serious prior allergic reaction to a penicillin
claims.quote: Penicillins are contraindicated in patients who have had serious allergic reactions to them.

claims.text: (or other beta-lactam, per the amox-clav and amp-sulbactam labels).
claims.quote: The use of UNASYN is contraindicated in individuals with a history of serious hypersensitivity reactions (e.g., anaphylaxis or Stevens-Johnson syndrome) to ampicillin, sulbactam or to other beta-lactam antibacterial drugs (e.g., penicillins and cephalosporins).

claims.text: Amox-clav/amp-sulbactam: prior cholestatic jaundice/hepatic dysfunction with that drug.
claims.quote: History of cholestatic jaundice/hepatic dysfunction associated with Amoxicillin and Clavulanate Potassium.

claims.text: Most patients who report penicillin allergy don't react on re-exposure;
claims.quote: Most patients who report an allergic reaction to penicillin do not react to subsequent exposure to penicillin.

claims.text: with a vague or inconsistent history and no effective or convenient alternative, skin testing may be done.
claims.quote: If patients have a vague or inconsistent history of penicillin allergy and taking alternative antibiotics is not effective or convenient, skin testing may be done.

claims.text: Probenecid blocks renal tubular secretion and raises penicillin levels.
claims.quote: Probenecid inhibits renal tubular secretion of many penicillins, increasing blood levels.
